messages:
maya: quick Q — we're remapping some AD groups to SCIM groups as part of the org cleanup. If a user is deprovisioned in AD and SCIM removes them, do we need to redact the user_id from logs or just pseudonymize? hoping for a quick security check before the deploy.

dan: fyi what logs are in scope? auth logs, audit logs, and request logs?

maya: mainly audit/event logs (sso provision events) and our request logs that include `user_id` in the debug payloads. not app-level PII elsewhere.

security-bot: automated-scan: last policy snapshot 2026-02-10 — rule SSO-LOG-01 flags raw user identifiers in request logs unless pseudonymized. See https://redwood-security/docs/sso-logging-policy

lina: short answer: redact the raw AD GUID in any non-audit retention logs. Audit trail (for compliance) should keep an immutable mapping in the audit store, but access-controlled. Pseudonymize in telemetry.

ops: we have a small PR open for the mapping change: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/412 — includes SCIM map + deprov hook. Might be easiest to add a transform in the hook to replace `user_id` with `user_hash`.

maya: thanks. here's the transform snippet I was planning to add to the deprov lambda:
```
const crypto = require('crypto');
function pseudonymize(id) {
  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(id + process.env.SALT).digest('hex').slice(0,16);
}
// before writing request logs: payload.user_id = pseudonymize(payload.user_id);
```

dan: that looks fine. a couple of notes: 1) SALT must be stored in KMS and rotated policy-defined, 2) ensure the audit store still records the mapping in an access-controlled table.

lina: agree with dan. Also add a short retention policy note in the PR description: where mappings live, who can access, and how long. compliance will ask.

maya: will do. for the mapping table — ops, do we have a documented access list?

ops: yes, we have an `sso-audit-admins` group in IAM. I'll include a link and add a small ACL check in the PR.

maya: one more thing — group remap rules: some users will move from `engineering-old` -> `engineering`. when SCIM removes old group, will that trigger deprov or just group change? want to avoid accidental deprovision.

dan: SCIM group deletion should not deprovision users if they are still in other groups that map to active roles. the deprov hook is only triggered on `active=false` or explicit `DELETE` user events. group-only changes are safe. :+1:

lina: can we add an integration test that simulates a group swap so we don't regress? small end-to-end in staging would be great.

maya: I'll add a test that sends SCIM PATCH group change and asserts no `DEPROVISION` event. will push to the PR today.

security-bot: audit-link: https://audit.internal/entries?search=1768579012 — created checklist: redact-in-telemetry, store-mapping-in-audit, kms-salt, acl-for-audit-table.

ops: thanks team — once PR is updated and tests pass I'll merge and schedule a canary. if anything unexpected re: logs we can rollback.

maya: thanks all :eyes: will update PR and tag you for review.
